direct_replay_observations: Player 2 issued 2467 Market build commands at map coordinate (110,35) from 12:53 through 40:39 and remained in Early Antiquity.
Player 1 first issued Militia-line production at 02:01.
Player 1 issued a Barracks build command at 00:00, a Lumber Camp at 01:01, and its first Mill at 03:55.
Player 1 issued Mill build commands at (21,140) and (23,146); Player 2 also placed its first two Mills about nine tiles apart.
Player 1 completed Middle Antiquity at 17:35, issued six Outpost builds before 18:08, a Monastery at 20:23, a second Town Center at 22:08, a University at 22:32, and completed Imperial at 30:14.
The land-attack timer refreshed repeatedly from 10:32 through 39:38, but no land-attack or periodic-attack dispatch message was recorded.
Both players issued only one Lumber Camp build command during the recorded match.
implementation_inferences: The unbounded fixed-position Market retry is sufficient to explain Player 2's villager churn and economic collapse.
Enemy armies on adjacent islands could be counted as local threats because the response scan lacked a mainland-reachability filter, potentially holding the attack system in home-defense state.
Phase-based desired Mill counts and the lack of a distinct-cluster requirement explain the nearby duplicate Mills.
Simultaneous Middle-Age optional-building goals competed with the second Town Center and Imperial reserve.
Animal-worker abandonment is consistent with automatic builder assistance and phase gatherer rebalancing, but the replay's WORK records do not identify individual villagers.
changes_under_test: Bound Market retries with pending checks, cooldowns, and a fallback placement mode.
Keep animal-food workers out of automatic builder assistance and raise the global resource-retask floor from 20 to the documented bounded maximum of 40 while shepherds or hunters are active.
Require an existing Mill and Lumber Camp (excluding queued foundations) before normal or rush Barracks construction and suppress generic Iron-Age Militia outside a selected drush.
Keep one planned Mill through the opening and require a distant food cluster for another.

Gate optional Middle-Age buildings behind a completed second Town Center, retain a 20-minute deadlock escape for required University and Monastery construction, and defer optional research while safely preparing Imperial.
Place a new Lumber Camp near a wood worker whose nearest camp is too distant.

Filter local defense threats to the AI's mainland, replace unreachable GROUP attack selections with the implemented PERCENTAGE executor, and correct assignment operators that made every land and naval attack-executor comparison false.
Launch up to three bounded scout-ferry missions to observed off-mainland land anchors after Middle Antiquity.
Disable villager sea-fish gathering and cap Fishing Ships by the existing desired-number-fishing goal.
fresh_replay_acceptance: No player repeats a failed Market placement more than three normal attempts plus one fallback per cooldown cycle.
Outside a selected drush, no Militia-line production occurs before Early Antiquity and Barracks construction follows completion of both the first Mill and Lumber Camp.
A second Mill is not attempted beside the opening Mill merely because the economy phase changed.

In a safe non-rush Middle age, the second Town Center precedes optional Outposts, Castle, and extra production buildings; University and Monastery also wait unless the 20-minute deadlock escape is reached.
A safe non-rush player starts Imperial research near the 15-to-20-minute target without optional research repeatedly spending the reserve.
Known adjacent-island units do not hold home defense active, and a sufficiently sized army dispatches an attack or transport assault.

After 10 minutes and Middle Antiquity, a scout is ferried when an observed off-mainland anchor and an unreserved transport exist; the mission is counted only after the scout is found unloaded on that land mass.
Shepherd and deer or boar hunter churn is materially lower while animal food remains, without freezing unrelated resource workers.
No land villager is assigned to sea fish, and the fishing fleet does not exceed desired-number-fishing.
known_limits: The replay parser does not yet decode research actions, so no individual technology is blamed for the delayed Imperial age.

The engine search API used here can select an observed off-mainland landing anchor but cannot deliberately select a completely black, unknown island; elapsed time is only a conservative scout trigger and does not prove the home island is fully explored.
Visible fish counts do not prove water-zone reachability from a Dock; a water-connectivity-aware fish controller remains unresolved.
The retask strategic numbers are global rather than per-role, so this change can only reduce animal-worker churn; a fresh replay must establish whether explicit phase balancing still reassigns them.
The mainland filter protects the original home land zone; defense of a later off-mainland colony needs separate zone ownership and remains unresolved.
Autonomous choke-point walling remains unresolved because the current wall code has no terrain-frontier or choke detector, and map classification alone is unsafe on Britannia-style island starts.
